sanskrit_verse: क्रमाद् ध्य एते प्रपद्येरन् मृते पितरि तद्धनम् । ज्यायसो ज्यायसोऽभावे जघन्यस्तदवाप्नुयात् ॥
transliteration: kramād dhy ete prapadyeran mṛte pitari taddhanam | jyāyaso jyāyaso 'bhāve jaghanyas tad avāpnuyāt ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Upon the father's death, his wealth shall devolve in order to his sons; in the absence of elder sons, the next in seniority shall receive it, and in their absence, the youngest shall inherit.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through lineage and designated succession
Causation is determined by natural order and ontological positioning
Capacity-based responsibility aligns with birth-order and readiness for stewardship
Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial dharma and material integrity
Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful assumption of ancestral duty
executable_legal_axioms: IF father is deceased AND sons exist THEN wealth transfers to eldest son FIRST
IF eldest son is absent THEN transfer to next eldest in line
IF no elder sons survive THEN youngest surviving son receives full inheritance
NO external claimant may interrupt bloodline succession without explicit prior designation
SUCCESSOR must acknowledge responsibility before assuming ownership
supreme_court_application: In matters of intestate succession, the Supreme Court shall uphold the primogeniture principle as reflective of dharma-ordained hierarchy. The court must verify ontological position within the family structure and ensure that any deviation from kramic order has clear, documented consent from the predecessor. Legal recognition follows spiritual readiness and familial alignment, not arbitrary preference.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This verse establishes pramāṇa-based succession rooted in anupūrvaśaḥ—sequential manifestation of authority through conscious lineage. Responsibility is proportionally aligned with positional dharma, not individual merit. There is no punitive framework; rather, misalignment disrupts cosmic harmony, which self-corrects when proper order is restored through rightful assumption.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process where all heirs publicly affirm understanding of their roles
Facilitate responsibility assumption protocol wherein successor declares acceptance of ancestral duties
Reintegrate displaced consciousness through guided ritual acknowledgment of succession rights
Restore capacity by ensuring financial literacy and dharmic education prior to asset transfer
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Succession flows from consciousness, not contention. Dharma prevails through rightful order. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
